title: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018 — overview
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, No. 5 of 2018
content: The Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act criminalises unauthorised access, interception, fraud, identity theft, and publication of false or intimate content. Preserve device logs, screenshots with URLs and dates, and report promptly to police or DCI. Do not delete evidence.

title: Data Protection Act, 2019 — overview
content: The Data Protection Act regulates collection and use of personal data, requiring lawful basis, purpose limitation, and data subject rights including access, correction, and deletion. Controllers and processors may need to register with the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner. Keep consent records and data policies.

title: Defamation on social media — general guidance
citation: Defamation Act, Cap. 36; Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act
content: False published statements harming reputation may lead to civil defamation claims or criminal complaints for false publications. Preserve posts, shares, and harm evidence, seek retraction in writing first, and verify deadlines with a lawyer before filing.

title: Employee and customer data for businesses — general guidance
content: Businesses holding staff or customer data should limit collection, secure records, and honour access and deletion requests. CCTV and marketing messages need clear notices and opt-outs. Keep consent forms and breach response records.

title: Phone theft and IMEI blocking — general guidance
citation: Kenya Information and Communications Act; CA guidance
content: After phone theft, report to police with the IMEI, notify the provider to block the SIM, and request device blocking where available. Keep purchase receipts, box IMEI, and police abstract for insurance or recovery.

title: M-Pesa andSIM-swap fraud — general guidance
citation: Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018; CBK guidance
content: For mobile money fraud, immediately reverse where possible, call the provider to freeze, report to police and DCI with transaction IDs, and notify your bank. Keep SMS records, transaction codes, and call reference numbers. Never share PINs or OTPs.

title: ODPC complaints — general guidance
content: Individuals whose data is misused can complain first to the organisation holding the data, then to the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner with evidence and reference numbers. Keep screenshots, messages, and the organisation's response for the complaint file.

title: Online harassment and intimate images — general guidance
content: Sharing intimate images without consent, cyberbullying, and threats are offences. Preserve links, screenshots with timestamps, and account handles, report to the platform and police, and seek support services. Requests for intimate content from strangers should be blocked and reported.

title: Securing M-Pesa and bank accounts
content: Use PINs, biometrics, and SIM PINs with no sharing of OTPs, and lock SIM swaps with the provider. Keep provider security confirmations.

title: Requesting your data from a company
content: Write to the data controller describing the data sought with ID; they must respond within statutory timelines. Escalate to ODPC where ignored. Keep delivery proof.

title: Agents photocopying IDs at shops
content: Question bulk ID copying at agents and shops; ask the purpose and retention. Sign across copies shared. Keep a log of copies given.

title: Protecting bank statements shared for jobs
content: Share redacted statements where possible and mark the purpose in writing. Demand deletion after review. Keep transmission records.

title: Biometric data at work and gates
content: Fingerprints and face data need explicit consent with secure storage and alternatives. Query necessity in writing. Keep consent and policy records.

title: What to do after a data breach notice
content: Change passwords, enable 2FA, monitor accounts, and preserve breach notices for claims. Report misuse to ODPC and DCI. Keep notices and loss records.

title: Recording calls as evidence
content: Recordings are weighed with consent, disclosure, and authenticity context. Get advice before secret recording. Keep originals with metadata.

title: Home CCTV and neighbours privacy
content: Angle cameras to your property, inform visitors, and secure footage with limited retention. Neighbour complaints go to ODPC. Keep signage photos and retention policy.

title: Workplace CCTV notices
content: Employers must post CCTV notices with purpose and retention, limiting coverage of private areas. Raise objections in writing. Keep notices and policies.

title: Church and chama member lists
content: Groups need consent before publishing member contacts or photos. Request removal in writing. Keep consent and removal records.

title: Valid consent for data collection
content: Consent must be freely given, specific, and informed with clear opt-in, not pre-ticked boxes. Withdraw anytime. Keep consent screens and withdrawal proof.

title: Defamation in WhatsApp groups
content: False group messages harming reputation attract civil and criminal complaints. Preserve full-chat exports with dates, seek retraction first. Keep harm evidence.

title: Deleting your data (right to erasure)
content: Request deletion where data is unnecessary or consent is withdrawn, subject to legal retention duties. Keep the request, response, and confirmation.

title: Doxxing: personal details posted online
content: Request platform removal, tighten account privacy, and report to ODPC and DCI with links. Keep removal requests and references.

title: Your rights over personal data
content: Data subjects can access, correct, delete, object, and withdraw consent with requests to the controller. Respond in writing with ID. Keep request and response copies.

title: Hacked email recovery
content: Recover via provider flows, revoke sessions, and check forwarding rules set by attackers. Warn banks linked to the email. Keep recovery logs.

title: Employer monitoring of staff
content: Workplace CCTV, email, and device monitoring need notice, policy, and proportionality. Challenge covert surveillance in writing. Keep policies and monitoring notices.

title: False publications about you online
content: False online publications are reported to platforms and DCI with links, timestamps, and harm evidence. Keep preservation screenshots before deletion.

title: GPS tracking by employers or spouses
content: Covert vehicle or phone tracking needs lawful basis and notice; challenge misuse in writing. Keep tracking evidence and objections.

title: Hospital records confidentiality
content: Health facilities must keep treatment records confidential with access on consent or court order. Request your records in writing. Keep request and disclosure logs.

title: Hotel guest registers
content: Hotels collect IDs per law but must secure registers and limit access. Query over-collection. Keep booking confirmations.

title: eCitizen and Huduma data safety
content: Use official eCitizen channels with strong passwords and verified agents; never share OTPs. Report misuse with transaction references. Keep payment receipts.

title: Signing across ID copies
content: Write the purpose and date across ID copies shared with agents to deter reuse for loans. Keep a log of copies issued.

title: Blocking a stolen phone by IMEI
content: Request IMEI blocking through the provider and police with box and purchase proof. Keep the box IMEI, receipt, and OB copy.

title: Job applicant data and background checks
content: Background checks need consent with relevant scope; demand to see adverse findings. Keep application copies and consent records.

title: Fake jobs harvesting ID data
content: Scam recruiters collect IDs and fees for nonexistent jobs. Verify premises and registration before sharing documents. Report with adverts and messages.

title: Children safety online
content: Use parental controls, approve apps, and teach reporting of strangers and explicit content. Report exploitation to DCI child units. Keep device and incident logs.

title: KRA PIN used by fraudsters
content: Check iTax for unknown obligations, change credentials, and report to KRA and DCI with affidavits. Keep dispute letters and references.

title: Legal aid for privacy violations
citation: Legal Aid Act; Data Protection Act
content: Victims of serious data misuse can seek NLAS help with evidence and references. The toll-free line is 0800 720 640. Keep the full evidence file.

title: Loan apps accessing contacts
content: Loan apps must limit collection and get consent before contacting your list; report shaming to ODPC and CBK. Keep permission screenshots and abusive messages.

title: Lost phone with mobile money
content: Block the SIM immediately, freeze mobile money, and report to police with IMEI. Remotely secure accounts where possible. Keep OB and provider references.

title: Stopping spam SMS and calls
content: Opt out with STOP codes, block senders, and report persistent spam to CA and ODPC. Keep spam samples and complaint numbers.

title: Getting M-Pesa statements for cases
content: Request certified statements through official channels with ID for the disputed period. Courts admit certified records. Keep request receipts and statements.

title: Filing a complaint with ODPC
content: Complain first to the organisation, then to ODPC with evidence, reference numbers, and timelines. File online with attachments. Keep the complaint reference.

title: Never share OTPs with callers
content: Banks, Safaricom, and KRA never ask for OTPs by phone. End suspicious calls and verify via official channels. Keep call details for DCI reports.

title: Password and account recovery hygiene
content: Use unique passwords with authenticator backups and updated recovery contacts. Store sparingly offline. Keep recovery codes safely.

title: Spotting phishing messages
content: Fake KRA, bank, and delivery links harvest credentials; verify sender addresses and never enter PINs via links. Report to providers and DCI. Keep message screenshots.

title: Removing personal data from public posts
content: Request search and platform delisting of exposed IDs, contacts, and addresses with evidence. Keep removal requests and outcomes.

title: Intimate images shared without consent
content: Report to platforms, police, and support services immediately with links and handles; do not engage the poster. Preserve evidence with timestamps. Keep report references.

title: SACCO member data use
content: Societies must limit statements sharing and get consent for marketing. Object to guarantor shaming. Keep objection letters.

title: CCTV in schools
content: Schools need CCTV policies with notices, limited coverage, and secure footage. Raise concerns with the board in writing. Keep policies and incident notes.

title: School records and children data
citation: Data Protection Act; Basic Education Act
content: Schools need parental consent for publishing pupil photos and limit access to records. Object in writing to misuse. Keep consent forms and publications.

title: Debt collectors contacting your family
content: Collectors must not disclose your debt to contacts; report shaming to ODPC and CBK. Keep abusive messages and call logs.

title: SIM replacement fraud prevention
content: Replace SIMs in person with original ID and secret questions; set a SIM PIN after. Report suspicious replacements immediately. Keep agent receipts.

title: Stalking and persistent harassment
citation: Protection Against Domestic Violence Act; Penal Code
content: Log every contact attempt with dates, seek protection orders, and report to police. Keep messages, logs, and witness details.

title: Children images in shows and adverts
content: Using children in adverts needs parental consent with contracts and limited hours. Keep consent forms and contracts.

title: Landlord handling of tenant IDs
content: Landlords should copy only needed ID pages, store securely, and return on exit. Object to sharing with third parties. Keep handover records.

title: Hacked WhatsApp accounts
content: Alert contacts, re-verify with SMS codes, enable two-step verification, and report fraud to contacts and DCI. Keep recovery records.

title: Public Wi-Fi safety
content: Avoid banking on open Wi-Fi, use VPNs, and verify hotspot names with staff. Log out of shared devices. Keep incident notes where losses follow.

title: Protecting witness contacts
content: Share witness details only with investigators and counsel, redacting where possible. Keep disclosure logs and protection references.
